evidence_families._definition: Which FAMILY of instrument produced a fact. Independence is a property of the INSTRUMENT, not of the tool id and not of this label: two capabilities that drive the same instrument are ONE opinion however they are labelled, and two different decompilers are also one opinion (fact_types.evidence_source says exactly this). The enumerated values below are the permitted set; R18 fails the run on anything else, and R18 also fails when two capabilities sharing one instrument declare different families. Correcting a label here cannot change what the mission gate believes about independence -- the gate must derive the family axis from the instrument -- but a registry that disagrees with itself is a registry nobody can reason about.
evidence_families.decompiler: reconstructs executable code into a higher-level language: Hex-Rays IDA and Ghidra both land here, and two of them agreeing is ONE opinion held twice, not corroboration
evidence_families.static-analysis: NOT a separate family. Retained only so the value is not silently re-used; no capability should carry it, because on this estate it existed solely to relabel one idalib-mcp capability and thereby manufacture a second family
evidence_families.dynamic-observation: watches a running subject: a live page over CDP, a live process
evidence_families.dynamic-instrumentation: injects into or attaches to a live process to observe or alter it
evidence_families.structural-parser: decodes a self-describing container without executing it: JOSE/JWT, zip, png
evidence_families.capture-analysis: reads recorded traffic rather than live traffic
evidence_families.artefact-parser: reads host artefacts left on disk: prefetch, SRUM, registry hives
evidence_families.package-inspection: reads a packaged artefact as built: APK manifest, DEX, resources
evidence_families.binary-similarity: matches functions across two binaries by scoring, without proving equivalence
evidence_families.differential-oracle: compares two implementations of the same parser and treats a disagreement as the finding
evidence_families.practice: solving self-built exercises; proves technique, not transfer
evidence_families.disassembler: reconstructs a machine instruction stream WITHOUT lifting it to a high-level language: capstone and similar code-generation libraries. Distinct from 'decompiler' because it performs no lifting, no type recovery and no control-flow reconstruction -- it is the only family here that states an OPERAND WIDTH, which is measured, not assumed: see native.disasm.capstone's negative control and the pairing study. Added 2026-10-02 after measuring that capstone independently identified the exact addresses Ghidra left as unresolved DAT_ references AND carried the byte-vs-dword width that Ghidra's output omitted. THIS IS NOT THE static-analysis RELABEL ESCAPE: that escape re-declared ONE instrument under a second name, which R18 also blocks by instrument identity. capstone is a genuinely different library with no decompiler in its lineage. What it does NOT buy is confirmation of MEANING -- it corroborates structure and operands, not what the code does.

A capability here states what it consumes, the typed facts it produces, what it requires, what it proves, what it does NOT prove, and a negative control that must fail. 'state: observed' means the probe below was actually run; the summary is what it printed. Verify with: python scripts/registry-verify.py. The honest member of the closed set is structural-parser -- a self-describing container decoded without executing it -- which is where packer identification genuinely sits: Die reads the PE container and its section names and matches signatures over them. It shares that family with native.pe.container and crypto.jose.parse, and those are DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS, so R18 is satisfied and correctly so. Two instruments in one family is not two opinions about a decompilation either, so this entry adds no corroboration to the independence gate and is not offered as any.
capabilities.root_reason: Genuine root. It is handed a path and answers a question about that file's container before anything else is allowed to run -- nothing upstream produces a packer verdict, and nothing downstream may trust one that was not produced here. capabilities.title: Disassemble a self-built PE at an RVA and resolve RIP-relative operands WITH their widths, using no decompiler at all
capabilities.scope_note: SELF-AUTHORED TARGETS. It reads a PE with pefile, maps an RVA through the section table, and decodes bytes with capstone. It does not execute the target and does not lift instructions to a language. A non-executable section is REFUSED unless --force is passed.
capabilities.composition_note: WHY IT EXISTS, in one measurement. On crackme-corpus/out/c01-stringobf.exe main at RVA 0x1080: IDA Pro inlined the XOR key constants as 18/11/90 and 26/5/51; Ghidra left two of them as DAT_140017344 and DAT_140017342 with NO width, which is dangerous because read as the natural u32, DAT_140017342 is 734042; capstone, containing no decompiler whatsoever, emits `movzx r9d, byte ptr [rip+0x16259]` -> 0x140017342 byte=90 and `mov r8d, dword ptr [rip+0x16254]` -> 0x140017344 dword=11. Same values IDA propagated, plus the WIDTH, because the movzx prefix says byte and the bare mov says dword. **So it is not merely a second opinion on structure: it is the only one of the three instruments that states the fact whose absence made Ghidra's output a trap rather than merely incomplete.**

inputs.name: binary
inputs.note: a Windows PE. Measured: crackme-corpus/out/c01-stringobf.exe.

inputs.name: function
inputs.note: consumed as the RVA SOURCE only. The image-space address is NOT usable here and must be rebased: this tool takes --rva, never an address, because passing an address to a file-offset mapping is the mistake documented in does_not_prove.

facts.note: the decoded instruction stream as {addr, mnemonic, op_str} triples. Measured 40 instructions from RVA 0x1080, including `cmp dword ptr [rsp + 0xa0], 2` at 0x1400010a2 -- the argc==2 guard the decompilers both report as `if (argc == 2)`.

every RIP-relative memory operand resolved to an absolute address WITH ITS WIDTH: {at, text, target, width, byte, dword}. This is the unique contribution. Measured: 0x140017342 width=byte value 90; 0x140017344 width=dword value 11; 0x140017343 width=byte value 51; 0x140017364 width=dword value 5.
the containing section and whether IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE (0x20000000) is set. Measured .text 0x60000020 executable, .rdata 0x40000040 not.

requires.install_note: Already installed in the system Python 3.14.7. No install, no disk cost. pefile 2024.8.26 is the same interpreter.

reach.proc_spawn_note: Declared because the probe and both controls invoke `python native-lab/tools/disasm.py` as a child process, which is the station's own interpreter reading a file. Nothing else spawns and no target executes -- exec_target stays false and that is the distinction the validator exists to keep honest.

proves: THAT A NON-DECOMPILER INSTRUMENT INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATES THE STRUCTURE of a locate claim. Measured with no decompiler in the lineage: `cmp dword ptr [rsp+0xa0], 2` at 0x1400010a2, and two calls to 0x140001000 with edx=0x12 and edx=0x1a -- matching the decompiled `argc == 2` guard and the decode-call lengths 18 and 26 that BOTH decompilers report.

THAT IT RESOLVES WHAT A DECOMPILER LEAVES BEHIND, INCLUDING THE WIDTH. The four RIP-relative operands it reports point at exactly the addresses Ghidra emitted as unresolved DAT_ references (0x140017342, 0x140017344, 0x140017343, 0x140017364) and it states that 0x140017342 is a BYTE load and 0x140017344 a DWORD load. Ghidra stated neither address's value nor its width; IDA stated the value but only by propagating a constant and discarding the width evidence.

THAT IT REFUSES NON-CODE. Measured: --rva 0x17000 lands in .rdata (Characteristics 0x40000040, no IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE) and returns exit 2 with the section name and its characteristics, where the first version of this tool returned ok:true with 8 instructions decoded out of ASCII string bytes.
does_not_prove: WHAT THE CODE MEANS. These are instructions, not recovered logic: no lifting, no types, no control-flow reconstruction. It corroborates that a comparison and two calls exist at these addresses; it cannot say the program checks a password.

THAT THE ACCEPTANCE MISSION NOW CONFIRMS, and this is the honest limit. evidence_source is 'disassembler', a genuinely different family from 'decompiler', so a chain of IDA plus capstone would satisfy the gate's two-instrument two-family requirement. **Whether that is CORRECT depends on the claim, and the gate cannot currently tell claims apart.** For 'main compares argc to 2 and calls a decode routine twice', capstone genuinely corroborates and confirmation would be honest. For 'the XOR key is 11, 90, 5, 51', it also happens to corroborate here -- but only because constant propagation happens to be visible in the operand, and that is a property of this binary, not a general guarantee. Registering this family must not be read as having resolved the acceptance question, and the mission's unresolved verdict stands until someone runs the chain and reads whether the RESULT is defensible, not merely whether the gate turned green.

THAT AN RVA IS AN ADDRESS. --rva takes a relative virtual address and maps it through the section table. Passing an image-space address, or using an RVA as a raw file offset, yields zero instructions or garbage; the first draft of this script did exactly that and the wrapper now refuses rather than reporting an empty success.
ANYTHING ABOUT A THIRD-PARTY BINARY. Corpus targets only.

THAT ADDING THIS FAMILY RESOLVED THE ACCEPTANCE MISSION. MEASURED, AND IT DID NOT. The Q2.locate acceptance mission was re-run AFTER this entry and the `disassembler` family existed in the schema, and it still returned tier=unresolved with independence FAIL: '2 capabilities resolve to 1 instrument(s) [idalib-mcp] carrying 1 distinct family/families [decompiler]'. The planner never routed this entry, because it has no `invoke` block -- the same condition that leaves native.function.match, native.pe.packer and native.crosscompare.ghidra probeable but uncallable. **So four capabilities in this registry, including the only instrument in a genuinely different family, cannot be planned into a mission.** That is the correct outcome -- registering a family must not be able to turn a gate green on its own -- and it is also the next structural hole. Wiring this one would require the typed edge to carry an RVA, because this tool takes --rva and IDA's native.func.addr is an image-space address, so the conversion has to happen somewhere and putting it in the argv would be the joined-command-line pattern R10 exists to refuse.

THAT A NAME LOOKUP IS ALWAYS UNAMBIGUOUS. THE POSITIONAL WEAKNESS IS CLOSED; THIS IS WHAT REPLACES IT. select.by_name='main' fails LOUDLY instead of guessing: measured, planting a name that does not exist makes round 4 SKIP with the missing name printed, independence drop back to '2 capabilities resolve to 1 instrument(s) [idalib-mcp] carrying 1 family', and the verdict return unresolved with a non-zero exit. So the confirmed result genuinely depends on capstone finding `main`; it cannot silently pick whatever sits at a position. Verified unambiguous on this binary: 362 functions, exactly one named `main` at 0x140001080, and NO duplicate names at all. THE RESIDUAL, stated rather than hidden: a binary with two overloads both named `main` would resolve to the first, and there is no disambiguation key. The `main` string is also a REGISTRY-SIDE HYPOTHESIS about which function the claim is about -- it is checked against the analyser's own recovered name, which is the strongest available check without a semantic claim-to-function binding, and that binding is not built.
gate_must_not_delegate: disasm.py against any binary this repository did not author
passing --force on a section that is merely suspicious rather than known to hold unpacked code
reading decoded instructions as recovered logic, or their presence as evidence a function is reachable
using an instruction count as a measure of function size: count stops at --count, not at the ret
capabilities.gate_must_not_delegate_why: Measured or read. (1) The target side is a red line. (2) --force is the one path that defeats the executable-section gate, and it exists for packed or self-modifying code where the section flags genuinely lie; used casually it restores exactly the garbage-out-of-data behaviour the gate exists to stop. (3) Reachability is a runtime property: native.crosscompare.ghidra and the frida entries both measured that the address being decodable and the address being executed are different questions. (4) --count truncates arbitrarily, so the count says nothing about the function's extent.

capabilities.evidence_source_note: A NEW family value, added to schema.evidence_families on 2026-10-02 with its definition written in. It is deliberately NOT the 'static-analysis' relabel escape: that escape re-declared ONE instrument under a second name, and R18 independently fails when two capabilities sharing one instrument declare different families. capstone is a different library with no decompiler in its lineage, and it was measured carrying evidence neither decompiler emitted. THE HONEST CAVEAT, which is the whole reason this note is long: family-level independence is CLAIM-BLIND. It asks whether two families spoke, not whether they agreed about the thing being claimed. Here they did agree, and that agreement was verified rather than assumed -- but the gate cannot tell a structural claim from a semantic one, so adding this family makes confirmation POSSIBLE, not automatically CORRECT. UPDATE 2026-10-02, after wiring: the Q2.locate acceptance mission now returns tier=confirmed with exit 0, independence reporting '3 capabilities across 2 instruments (capstone, idalib-mcp) carrying 2 distinct family/families [decompiler, disassembler]'. That was NOT obtained by weakening any gate -- independence, process and the rest are unchanged in strength and the mission's own 51-control selftest still passes, including the forged-evidence-id case. It was obtained by making a real, already-measured instrument routable. The conversion from image-space address to RVA happens INSIDE the wrapper, never in this argv, because R10 exists precisely to refuse commands assembled by string concatenation and because ImageBase differs per binary -- 0x140000000 here -- so a caller computing it would be baking a per-target constant into a shared command.

select.note: SELECTED BY NAME, NOT BY POSITION. The first version of this entry used index 1, which I verified by hand was `main` on this binary -- and nothing in the chain checked it. Two instruments agreeing about an address they were both handed by position corroborates the bytes at that address, not the claim. select.by_name fails loudly instead: if no function carries that name the round is SKIPPED and named, rather than falling through to whatever sits at index 1. A gate that picks the wrong thing is worse than one that refuses. The remaining limit is honest: `main` is a registry-side hypothesis about which function the claim is about. It is checked against the analyser's own recovered name, which is the strongest available check without a semantic claim-to-function binding, and that binding is not built.

capabilities.title: Report whether a Windows PE carries an Authenticode certificate table, and decode its WIN_CERTIFICATE header -- without verifying anything
capabilities.scope_note: READ-ONLY on the target. Reads IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_SECURITY from the PE optional header and, if present, the WIN_CERTIFICATE header it points at. It never executes a target and never contacts a network: no revocation checking, no chain building, no OCSP, no CRL.
capabilities.composition_note: WHY IT IS THE CHEAPEST REAL EXPANSION OF THE THINNEST AXIS. Coverage measured 2026-10-02 across the seven question types showed Q6 -- 'what token/signature/key handling is this' -- resting on ONE instrument, crypto.jose.parse, which is JOSE/JWT only. For a Windows PE the signature handling lives in the same optional header native.pe.packer and native.pe.container already read, so this costs no new dependency, no install and no disk. The trap it encodes is the one that makes this non-obvious: IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_SECURITY's VirtualAddress is a FILE OFFSET, not an RVA, unlike every other data directory. Mapping it through the section table produces a plausible address in the wrong place.

inputs.name: binary
inputs.note: a Windows PE. Measured: crackme-corpus/out/c01-stringobf.exe.

facts.note: boolean: is a WIN_CERTIFICATE table present. Measured false for all seven corpus binaries (SECURITY VA=0x0 size=0) and true for a self-authored fixture. THIS IS NOT A TRUST VERDICT -- see does_not_prove.

the decoded WIN_CERTIFICATE: {header_offset, dwLength, wRevision, revision_is_2_0, wCertificateType, type_is_pkcs_signed_data, blob_offset, blob_len, blob_sha256_prefix, blob_ascii_head}. Measured on the fixture: offset 143872, dwLength 48, revision 0x200, type 0x2, blob reading back the authored ASCII.
the raw directory entry: {security_offset, security_size}, explicitly labelled as a FILE OFFSET. This is the fact a caller would get wrong by treating it as an RVA.

requires.install_note: Already installed. No install, no disk cost. Runs in ~0.15 s.

reach.proc_spawn_note: Declared because the probe and both controls invoke `python headless-lab/tools/authenticode.py` as a child process. Nothing else spawns, exec_target stays false, and no network is touched -- which is the property that matters here, since real revocation checking would need one.

proves: THAT A CERTIFICATE TABLE IS PRESENT OR ABSENT, on a self-authored fixture and on a real binary. Measured: the fixture returns signed:true with security_offset 143872, dwLength 48, wRevision 0x200, wCertificateType 0x2, and its blob reading back the authored ASCII marker; every corpus binary returns signed:false with an empty directory. Two inputs, opposite answers, from the same code -- which is the only thing that makes 'unsigned' mean anything.

THAT THE WIN_CERTIFICATE HEADER DECODES, and that the FILE-OFFSET semantics of IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_SECURITY are handled as such rather than as an RVA. That distinction is the whole reason this is an entry rather than four lines in triage.md.
does_not_prove: THAT THE BINARY IS TRUSTED, OR THAT ITS SIGNATURE IS VALID. NOTHING IS VERIFIED. No chain is built, no certificate is parsed, no hash is recomputed over the image, no revocation is checked, no timestamp is examined. `signed: true` means exactly 'there is a WIN_CERTIFICATE here'. A binary whose image was modified after signing still reads signed:true here, and the self-authored fixture reads signed:true with no key and no signature at all. Any trust decision needs a tool that actually verifies, and this is not one.
THAT AN ABSENCE MEANS UNSIGNED BY CHOICE. A repacked or tampered binary can have its certificate table stripped, which reads identically to one that was never signed. Absence is not provenance.
THAT THE PKCS#7 BLOB IS WELL FORMED. It is located and hashed, not parsed. The blob_sha256_prefix is an identity, not a validation.
ANYTHING ABOUT A THIRD-PARTY BINARY. Corpus targets only.
gate_must_not_delegate: authenticode.py against any binary this repository did not author
reporting pe.signed as a trust or integrity result, or as evidence a binary is unmodified
treating pe.signed:false as evidence a binary was never signed rather than possibly stripped
running --make-control over a real signed binary to 'see what it looks like': it rewrites the directory entry and would produce a fixture claiming to be signed by nothing
capabilities.gate_must_not_delegate_why: Measured or read. (1) The target side is a red line. (2) The verifies-nothing limitation is the single largest in this registry, and a caller who reads signed:true as integrity is worse off than one with no tool at all -- that is why the caveat travels in every payload as well as here. (3) A stripped certificate table is indistinguishable from a never-signed one without external provenance. (4) The fixture generator APPENDS to the file and REWRITES the directory entry, so pointed at a real signed binary it produces something that claims to be signed by nothing, which is the most dangerous artefact this tool can make.

negative_control.expect_output_note: TWO controls, because one is not enough and the second had to be built. (1) THE POSITIVE CASE, built because every corpus binary is unsigned -- all seven measured SECURITY VA=0x0 size=0 -- so without a fixture this entry could only ever report 'not signed' and would be an always-green check. The fixture is self-authored: an 8-byte WIN_CERTIFICATE header plus an ASCII marker, appended outside the sections with the data directory pointed at it. Measured signed:true, dwLength 48, wRevision 0x200, wCertificateType 0x2, blob reading back the authored string byte for byte. **It proves the PARSER fires and proves nothing about signatures; it is deliberately not a valid signature -- there is no key and none.** (2) THE FAILING CASE, which is the one the validator insisted on and the more valuable of the two: truncate the fixture so the directory still points at offset 143872 while the file is now 143860 bytes. A parser that trusted the directory entry would read past the end and either raise an opaque IndexError or return garbage; this one refuses with exit 2 and names both the offset and the real file size. **A signature surface is attacker-controlled data pointing into an attacker-controlled file, so 'the pointer is inside the file' is a boundary, not a formality.** Getting the directory entry written took two silent bugs worth recording: the offset was first computed arithmetically and landed 24 bytes into the optional header, leaving SECURITY at zero so the fixture read back unsigned with no error anywhere; and while correcting it the struct.pack_into call was deleted outright, so the certificate was appended and the entry never written. **A tool that builds a fixture it then cannot detect is exactly what these controls exist to catch, and both bugs produced precisely that.**
